Source-independent table structure

Source: R/TosiSchema.R
TosiStructure.Rd

TosiStructure describes a table or series through ordered components, identifiers, labels, roles, and available value domains. It retains language, frequency, and series-key information without requiring source identity or version. TosiSchema adds that source binding and inherits the structural methods. Fields are read-only; direct and nested replacement fails.

Component inspection

Use $component(id) for exact-ID lookup and $domain_table(id) for the complete domain. Each component also provides $domain_table() with the same return contract. component$domain_size() counts the stored primary domain vector without constructing a table: NA_integer_ when unavailable, 0L for a recorded empty domain.

Code domains may include note alongside code and label, with one note per code in the same order; missing entries and repeated notes are retained. A Dimension may also expose a read-only classification_id. Interpret it within its source, Dimension and version context, not as a globally stable identifier. $as_list() retains both facts, and $as_schema() preserves them while sharing components.

print(component) or component$print(n = 3) bounds displayed domain rows for Dimensions, Time, Frequency and unknown roles. Attributes show metadata and domain size only; Value shows its unit when recorded. Printing returns the same object invisibly without mutation. $domain_table() returns the complete domain regardless of display limits; truncation and omission markers are not literal source-filter values.

Use str(schema) or str(component) to inspect R6 fields and method signatures rather than the interactive overview. Component constructors are technical exports, not an extension interface.

Time construction accepts ranges = NULL, one time_range() value or a list of values with unique frequencies. $ranges is a read-only unnamed list in supplied order; $as_list()$ranges contains plain records with frequency strings and Date/POSIXct endpoints. Ranges do not populate $frequencies() or establish an enumerated Time domain.

TosiStructure$new()

Construct a structural schema from package-owned schema components.

Usage

TosiStructure$new(
  components,
  object_type = NULL,
  lang = NULL,
  frequency = NULL,
  series_key = NULL,
  observation_count = NULL,
  series_count = NULL
)

Arguments

components

Non-empty ordered list of package-owned schema component objects.

object_type

Optional connector-supplied object type: "table", "series", or NULL.

lang

Scalar natural-language code or "codes".

frequency

Optional scalar known frequency code.

series_key

Optional ordered character vector of eligible series-key component IDs.

observation_count

Optional actual observation count for this object's scope; NULL or NA_real_ means unknown.

series_count

Optional actual series count for this object's scope; NULL or NA_real_ means unknown.

Returns

A new TosiStructure object.

TosiStructure$frequencies()

Return the fixed frequency when present, otherwise the Frequency component's domain, without inference or retrieval.

Usage

TosiStructure$frequencies()

Returns

The existing frequency vector, preserving class, order, missing values and typed-empty values, or NULL when absent or unavailable.

TosiStructure$n_observations()

Report source-established actual observations for this object's scope or potential grid positions, not occupancy. Potential counts span logical axes including Time, counting canonical replacements once; Value, Attributes and scalar frequency are not axes. Neither kind falls back to the other or performs retrieval.

Usage

TosiStructure$n_observations(kind = c("actual", "potential"))

Arguments

kind

One of "actual" (default) or "potential".

Returns

One numeric count, or NA_real_ when unknown; a known empty grid is zero.

TosiStructure$n_series()

Report source-established actual series for this object's scope or potential grid positions across the resolved series_key, not occupancy. An unavailable key is unknown; an empty key has one slot. Neither kind falls back to the other or performs retrieval.

Usage

TosiStructure$n_series(kind = c("actual", "potential"))

Arguments

kind

One of "actual" (default) or "potential".

Returns

One numeric count, or NA_real_ when unknown; a known empty grid is zero.

TosiStructure$as_schema()

Create a new source-bound schema with the supplied binding, retaining actual counts and sharing existing component instances without cloning. The receiver and its source binding, if any, remain unchanged.

Usage

TosiStructure$as_schema(connector_id, object_id, data_version)

Arguments

connector_id

Scalar canonical connector ID.

object_id

Scalar canonical object ID.

data_version

Finite non-missing scalar POSIXct source version.

Returns

A new TosiSchema object.

TosiStructure$print()

Print a compact overview without domain values. Dimensions, Time, Frequency and unknown roles appear together; Attributes and Value are summarized separately. Relative order within each group is preserved, without changing stored component order. Domain sizes distinguish unrecorded from recorded empty domains.

Usage

TosiStructure$print()

Returns

This schema object, invisibly and without mutation.

TosiStructure$component()

Look up a component by its exact ID, not a list name, label, role or position. An unknown ID raises a lookup error.

Usage

TosiStructure$component(id)

Arguments

id

Exact component ID.

Returns

The existing schema component object, without cloning.

TosiStructure$domain_table()

Return a component's complete domain by delegating to its $domain_table() method. An unknown ID raises a lookup error. Domain values are not translated into source filters; filter conventions are source-specific.

Usage

TosiStructure$domain_table(id)

Arguments

id

Exact component ID.

Returns

A tibble in source order with code and optional label/note, time, or frequency columns, preserving vector types including native Date/POSIXct and frequency values. Returns NULL for an unrecorded domain (including Value), or a typed zero-row tibble for a recorded empty domain.

TosiStructure$column_names()

Return physical column names in component order without changing the structure. "labels" uses component labels, "safe_labels" converts them to safe IDs, and "ids" uses canonical component IDs. Label modes fall back to IDs with a warning when labels are blank, protect canonical Time and Value names, and repair collisions across the complete structure, including undelivered Attributes.

Usage

TosiStructure$column_names(col_mode = c("labels", "safe_labels", "ids"))

Arguments

col_mode

One of "labels", "safe_labels", or "ids".

Returns

A character vector of physical names named by component ID.

TosiStructure$as_list()

Return the schema as a named list, with components as named lists. Count groups always contain both actual and potential; unknown counts are retained as NULL entries.

Usage

TosiStructure$as_list()

Returns

A named list containing the schema fields, components and observation_count and series_count groups.

TosiStructure$clone()

The objects of this class are cloneable with this method.

Usage

TosiStructure$clone(deep = FALSE)

Arguments

deep

Whether to make a deep clone.
